issues.title: Missing Vandermonde nonsingularity in the chain lemma

diagnostic_evidence.quote: We should note that, different from the scalar case, $B_{1},\dotsc,B_{d}$ having disjoint spectra is not sufficient to guarantee the nonsingularity of $\van$.

issues.failure_explanation: The lemma assumes disjoint real spectra and nonsingular terminal S_{i,d}, then begins its proof with a fundamental polynomial whose existence has not been established. For B_1=[[3,1],[-2,0]], B_2=[[2,-1],[2,5]], and B_3=[[19/3,-2/3],[2/3,14/3]], the spectra are respectively {1,2}, {3,4}, and {5,6}; the recurrence gives det(S_{2,3})=-1, det(S_{1,3})=-80, and S_{3,3}=I. Nevertheless, the block row [(16,7),(-16,2),(0,-9)] annihilates Van. A putative F_1 with coefficient block C must satisfy Van C=[I;0;0], but multiplication by this left-null row would require (16,7)=0. Thus F_1 does not exist under these admissible old hypotheses, and the proof invokes an undefined input.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem:Chain and its generic-k extension thm:Chain are not valid on singular-Vandermonde instances allowed by their old statements. Later results that explicitly assume Van nonsingular, or obtain it almost surely in the Gaussian regime, do not rely on the invalid extra scope.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Amend both lem:Chain and thm:Chain to assume that the block Vandermonde matrix Van in eq:defvand is nonsingular, equivalently after the block-row permutations used for general k. Invoke prop:interpolation before introducing the relevant fundamental matrix polynomial, while retaining the existing nonsingularity assumptions on the terminal S matrices and the factorization argument.
issues.why_classification: The proof genuinely needs a missing premise because disjoint spectra and nonsingular terminal S matrices do not ensure that the fundamental polynomial exists. Nevertheless, Vandermonde nonsingularity is a local rank/nondegeneracy qualification explicitly supported by the old interpolation and generic-nonsingularity results. Adding it to the lemma and its generic-k extension preserves their formulas, proof mechanism, and intended Gaussian regime, excluding only exceptional singular instances that do not propagate to later results.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Assuming that the matrix $\van$ in \cref{eq:defvand} is nonsingular, and all $S_{i,d}$ are nonsingular for $1\leq i\leq d$

issues.title: False d=2 condition-number bound for chi_mono
issues.failure_explanation: The display claims that the d=2 quantity chi_mono is at most max_i ||B_i||||B_i^{-1}||. The preceding old definition actually establishes that chi_mono is a maximum of endpoint ratios ||cI-B_i||/||cI-Lambda_i||. Take Lambda_1=diag(1000,1001), Omega_1=[[1,-10],[0,1]], Lambda_2=diag(998,999), and Omega_2=I. Then B_1=[[1000,10],[0,1001]], and at the endpoint c=1001 the first ratio is sqrt(101), whereas the maximum old right-hand condition number is approximately 1.0101. The strict violation persists under perturbation, so the Gaussian context does not rescue the displayed deterministic inequality. Similarity establishes instead that each ratio is bounded by ||Omega_i||||Omega_i^{-1}||.
issues.overall_effect: The d=2 discussion understates chi_mono and identifies conditioning of B_i, rather than conditioning of its eigenvector matrix Omega_i, as the relevant control. No formal result relies on this illustrative display.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the d=2 estimate by the endpoint-ratio formula from the definition of chi_mono and bound each ratio by ||Omega_i||||Omega_i^{-1}|| using cI-B_i=Omega_i^{-1}(cI-Lambda_i)Omega_i. Remove the unsupported bound involving ||B_i||||B_i^{-1}|| and identify eigenvector-matrix conditioning as the relevant control.
issues.why_classification: A short similarity argument supplies a complete local replacement, and no formal result or downstream guarantee requires reconstruction. However, the original substantive claim that chi_mono is controlled by the condition number of B_i is false and cannot be retained; the valid replacement uses the materially different condition number of Omega_i. The surviving d=2 conditioning discussion is recognizably comparable, so the loss is limited rather than major, but the changed control quantity prevents classification as a same-guarantee minor repair.

issues.title: Incorrect square-root exponent in the d=2 chi_coef formula
issues.failure_explanation: The d=2 display claims that chi_coef contains ||(B_1-B_2)^{-1}||^{1/2}. The old governing definition establishes the power 1/(d-1); at d=2 this is 1, so the supported specialization is ||(B_1-B_2)^{-1}|| times the minimum spectral separation. The square root changes both the value and scaling of the quantity.
issues.overall_effect: The illustrative d=2 formula misstates the defined coefficient-growth parameter, but the general definition and formal results remain unchanged.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the exponent 1/2 by 1, yielding chi_coef = ||(B_1-B_2)^{-1}|| times the minimum separation between Lambda_1 and Lambda_2.
issues.why_classification: The old governing definition uniquely gives the exponent 1/(d-1)=1 when d=2, and the subsequent discussion likewise uses the norm of the inverse without a square root. An adept reader can make this uniquely forced transcriptional correction directly, with no repair to any argument, definition, or dependent guarantee.

issues.title: Reciprocal norm substituted for norm of the inverse

failure_location.quote: Therefore, estimating $\norm{(B_{1}-B_{2})}^{-1}$ is as challenging  as analyzing RSBL.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: However, estimating $\chic$, or equivalently $\norm{(B_{1}-B_{2})^{-1}}$, is highly non-trivial since both $B_{1}$ and $B_{2}$ are \emph{nonsymmetric}.

issues.failure_explanation: The sentence literally claims that estimating the reciprocal ||B_1-B_2||^{-1} is as challenging as analyzing RSBL. The old paper actually establishes and repeatedly discusses the different quantity ||(B_1-B_2)^{-1}||, which depends on the smallest singular value rather than the largest singular value. The surrounding argument therefore supports only the corrected sentence.
issues.overall_effect: The concluding sentence of the intrinsic-challenge discussion names the wrong conditioning quantity; the preceding technical argument itself uses the correct norm of the inverse.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||B_1-B_2||^{-1} by ||(B_1-B_2)^{-1}|| in the concluding sentence.
issues.why_classification: The preceding discussion, the block-LU calculation, and the repeated identification of the relevant smallest-singular-value quantity uniquely force the norm of the inverse. Only the parentheses are misplaced; the reasoning already uses the correct object and requires no mathematical repair.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: Therefore, estimating $\norm{(B_{1}-B_{2})^{-1}}$ is as challenging  as analyzing RSBL.
